newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs talk with Boeing, McDonnell, CSA on Aero.
newsitem.headline: Czechs talk with Boeing, McDonnell, CSA on Aero.

text.p: The Czech government will hold exclusive talks with a consortium of Boeing Co, McDonnell Douglas and Czech airline Ceske Aerolinie a.s. for a 34-40 percent stake in Czech jet maker Aero Vodochody a.s., Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Wednesday.
Klaus said a final decision should be made on the sale by September. The aim of further negotiations would be to maximise the share of domestic supplies for Aero
"The interested party with which we will hold talks is the well-known consortium of Boeing Co , McDonnell Douglas and Czech airlines Ceske Aerolinie a.s," Klaus told a news conference.

Aero is developing a light subsonic fighter, the L-159, to be supplied to the Czech army. The Czech military has signed a letter of intent for the purchase of 72 L-159s, and Hungary has also shown interest.

State-controlled shareholders of the debt-strapped company approved a cut in Aero's basic capital to one million crowns from 962 million and subsequent underwriting of new shares in a financial restructuring plan.

The Czech government has declared it would sell a 34 to 40 percent stake in the troubled company to a financially strong strategic investor for a minimum of 950 million crowns, through an equity expansion. The cabinet must still decide how large the stake will be.
Other parties that had expressed an interest in Aero, include British Aerospace plc and Sweden's Saab bidding as part of the "Gripen" consortium, and the Czech investment company, CIMEX Holding a.s..
